content: Marcus Clement is a University of Washington Informatics student focused on data science. He builds practical things that make work easier — features, workflows, and automated systems. His work sits between software, data, and the people who use it. He enjoys owning problems end to end: sitting down with stakeholders to scope what they actually need, shipping a simple version, then iterating until it is reliable and genuinely useful. Lately that means architecting agentic AI systems on cloud infrastructure, plus the enablement work that gets people actually using them. Outside school and work he enjoys running, lifting, hiking, and golfing. Core skills: Applied AI, Agentic Automation, Cloud Architecture, Solutions Engineering, Full-Stack Development, Consulting. He also works in AI enablement and integration, solutions architecture, and prompt and context engineering.

Marcus attends the University of Washington (GPA 3.93) in Seattle, pursuing a B.S. in Informatics (Data Science) (Sep 2025 - Jun 2027). Before that he completed an Associate's in Arts and Sciences at Bellevue College (Sep 2023 - Jun 2025).

AI Systems Engineer Intern at Socratics.ai (Mar 2026 - May 2026) in Seattle, WA. Socratics.ai is a startup — Marcus has direct startup experience here. He engineered an AI document processing pipeline for financial data ingestion, model-driven classification, and human-in-the-loop (HITL) validation. He presented the AI workflow architecture to the executive team, defining automation strategy and feature priorities for production. Marcus originally consulted for Socratics.ai through the Business Impact Group and was invited back for a full internship based on his performance.

AI Product Engineer Intern at AirPLAi Sports (Jan 2026 - Mar 2026) in Seattle, WA. AirPLAi is a startup — Marcus has direct startup experience here. He engineered prompt and context strategies for a production AI chatbot, implementing guardrails and scoping new features. He built agent workflows and data retrieval logic in Python using LangGraph and FastAPI. He also implemented UI accessibility features for the sports AI chatbot, adding inline tooltip overlays for key term definitions.

Full Stack Developer at Web Impact UW (Jan 2026 - Jun 2026) in Seattle, WA. Developed features across React frontend, API routes, and backend, owning implementation to deployment under deadlines. Collaborated cross-functionally with design and product leads to deliver user-focused web solutions for external clients. Implemented UI components with shadcn and delivered maintainable code through GitHub workflows.

Member Service Agent at Costco Wholesale (Feb 2024 - Jun 2026) in Issaquah, WA. On the College Retention Program since Sep 2025. Assisted customers through complex issues via chat/phone, translating technical processes into clear explanations. Consistently exceeded performance expectations by over 50% through strong communication and problem-solving.

Data Science Intern at Everlane Landscaping (Jun 2025 - Aug 2025) in Kirkland, WA. Built automated Python pipeline to process 100+ monthly logs, optimizing routing and reducing job-time by 15%. Developed Tableau dashboards that improved reporting accuracy by 25%. Conducted data modeling to identify high-value customer segments, leading to 12% increase in customer retention.

Cursor-Inspired Portfolio (marcusclementportfolio.vercel.app). A personal portfolio that makes browsing feel familiar and intuitive to developers. Built with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript — no frameworks — and deployed on Vercel. Designed to mimic the Cursor IDE with a file explorer sidebar, tabbed editor pane, and AI chat panel. Features include drag-and-drop tab reordering, a resizable AI sidebar, and a fully functional AI chatbot.

The portfolio chatbot is powered by Claude Haiku 4.5 via the Anthropic API with RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation). It uses a structured JSON knowledge base with topic chunks covering Marcus's experience, projects, skills, and certifications. When a user sends a message, keyword-based retrieval scores each chunk against the query and injects the top 3 most relevant chunks into the system prompt for grounded, accurate responses. Responses are streamed in real time via Server-Sent Events (SSE) through a Vercel serverless function. The backend includes rate limiting, CORS validation, input sanitization, and security headers. The frontend features starter prompts, auto-scroll during streaming, and an info modal explaining the architecture. The entire implementation uses no frameworks — just vanilla JavaScript on the frontend and a single serverless function on the backend.

Personal Productivity System — Custom Obsidian Dashboard (Apr 2026 - Jun 2026). Marcus built a custom dashboard aggregating task management, goal tracking, and live health metrics in a single view. He integrated the WHOOP and Strava REST APIs using OAuth 2.0 with automated token refresh, building a Python/Bash launchd pipeline to sync daily sleep, recovery, activities, and HRV metrics. He deployed a Dockerized MCP server to connect Claude AI to the vault, enabling natural language note management and file operations. He built an AI-generated daily training brief using the Claude API, synthesizing recovery scores, pace history, and weekly mileage into a personalized coaching summary delivered automatically each morning. He embedded a live Google Calendar day view by registering an OAuth 2.0 client in Google Cloud Console and configuring API scopes and redirect URIs. The projects page has an expandable screenshots folder showing the Home Base page, daily brief, schedule, sleep and recovery view, last run, to-do and goals, and a 28-day habit grid.

Nick-Blendz.com — Online Booking Application (Jun 2025 - Jul 2025). Built and deployed a full-stack booking platform with Next.js, TypeScript, and AWS (EC2, S3, RDS) supporting 100+ users. Designed the database schema and backend to manage scheduling and client data, cutting manual booking work by 80%. Integrated scheduling API and analytics dashboards.

Medi-Scribe — AI Medical Transcription System (Sep 2025 - Dec 2025). Architected a HIPAA-compliant medical transcription pipeline on AWS (S3, Lambda, Transcribe Medical, Bedrock) and React. Automated clinical documentation workflows for doctor-patient interactions, improving transcription efficiency end to end.

Document Management System (Jun 2024 - Jul 2024). Built a PostgreSQL-based document management system for a real estate investor. Designed a relational schema and SQL backend using JSON to streamline property and record management.

AWS Certifications (3x): Solutions Architect Associate (SAA-C03), Cloud Practitioner (CLF-C02), AI Practitioner (AIF-C01). Azure Certifications (3x): AZ-900 (Azure Fundamentals), AI-900 (Azure AI Fundamentals), DP-900 (Azure Data Fundamentals). That is 6 cloud certifications total. He is currently preparing for the AWS Gen AI Developer certification.

Languages & backend: Python, R, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, FastAPI. Frontend: React, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, HTML & CSS. Tools: Git, GitHub, Docker, Vercel. Cloud: AWS, Azure, GCP. Data & analytics: SQL, Snowflake, Tableau, Power BI, Excel. AI: Amazon Q Business, Quick Suite, Gemini Gems, LangGraph, MCP, RAG, Claude Code. LLMs: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini.

Marcus has done extensive research on Amazon Q Business and Quick Suite (two distinct AWS products) and studied many demos on best practices for both. With Amazon Q Business he knows how to build custom chatbots grounded in enterprise data using connectors, and with Quick Suite he knows how to create workflows and agentic experiences. Across both he understands how to leverage features like connectors, MCP, and best practices in agentic workflows.
Marcus has played around with Gemini Gems on his personal account and has watched demos on the enterprise version. He has seen hands-on how to work with that tool.
Email: marcus20@uw.edu. LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/marcus-clement27.

Community involvement: Business Impact Group (Consultant, Jan-Mar 2026, collaborated with Socratics.ai and was invited back for internship), Web Impact UW (Full Stack Developer), NetworkAI (Director of Technology, leading AI workshops and all club tech events), Kappa Theta Pi (professional technology fraternity, worked in cross-functional team to create and deploy fraternity webpage), AWS Cloud Club (member, building projects and attending workshops/hackathons), Claude Builder Club (member, building projects and attending workshops/hackathons), Newman Center (Student Ministry Team Member since Sep 2025).

Volunteering: Strategy Consultant at Ronald McDonald House (Jul 2026) — participated in the RMHC Bay Area x Proofpoint Hackathon to redesign the Comfort & Joy Holiday Drive, a program delivering 10,000+ toys annually to families of critically ill children across the Bay Area. Basketball Camp Counselor at Liberty Sr High School (Jun 2022) — assisted with the annual Liberty Select Basketball Camp for K-8 students. Basketball Coach at Upward Sports (Jan 2019 - Mar 2019) — coached a 5th-6th grade youth basketball team through a full season. These roles show Marcus gives back through both strategy/consulting work for nonprofits and hands-on youth mentorship and coaching.

The portfolio is designed to mimic the Cursor IDE interface with a dark theme. It has three main panels: a file explorer sidebar on the left listing pages as files (about.md, experience.md, projects.md, etc.), a central editor pane with a tab system for switching between pages, and an AI chat sidebar on the right. Users can drag and drop to reorder tabs, resize the AI panel, and interact with the chatbot. The site is fully responsive — on mobile it collapses to a single-column layout. All content is rendered client-side from a JavaScript data object with no build step or framework.

Outside of school and work, Marcus enjoys running, lifting, hiking, and golfing (even though he admits he's not great at it yet). He's active and outdoorsy, and balances his technical work with physical activities.
